original_question: If a metric space (X, d) is pseudocomplete, must its Wijsman hyperspace (2^X, T_W(d)) also be pseudocomplete? Likewise, if (X, d) is subcompact or base-compact, must (2^X, T_W(d)) inherit the corresponding property?
target_in_paper: Section 3, Question 3.11: "If (X, d) is pseudocomplete (resp. subcompact, base-compact), must (2^X, T_W(d)) be pseudocomplete (resp. subcompact, base-compact)?"
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper’s exact target. It identifies the right section of the paper (the completeness-type-properties discussion), keeps the correct direction of implication from the metric space to its Wijsman hyperspace, and names exactly the three properties that appear in the official question: pseudocomplete, subcompact, and base-compact. It also correctly uses the Wijsman hyperspace notation (2^X, T_W(d)) and does not broaden the problem beyond what the paper asks.
missing_details: In this paper, 2^X means the family of all nonempty closed subsets of X, not the full power set of X.
The topology on the hyperspace is specifically the Wijsman topology T_W(d) induced by the given metric d.
Pseudocomplete, subcompact, and base-compact are being used as topological properties of the metric topology T(d) on X; a stand-alone formulation should make that explicit.

The paper recalls pseudocompleteness in the Aarts-Lutzer sense: X is quasi-regular and has a sequence {P_n : n in N} of open π-bases such that every nested choice V_n in P_n with V_{n+1} ⊆ V_n for all n has nonempty intersection.

The paper uses subcompact and base-compact in the Amsterdam sense: existence of an open base B such that every regular filterbase in B, respectively every centered family in B, has nonempty intersection.

The official question asks only the three corresponding implications (pseudocomplete to pseudocomplete, subcompact to subcompact, base-compact to base-compact); it does not ask about countable or almost Amsterdam variants, nor does it impose extra hypotheses such as separability, local separability, or complete metrizability.
refined_question: Let (X, d) be a metric space, let 2^X denote the set of all nonempty closed subsets of X, and equip 2^X with the Wijsman topology T_W(d). If the metric topology T(d) on X is pseudocomplete, i.e. X is quasi-regular and has a sequence {P_n : n ∈ N} of open π-bases such that every sequence V_n with V_n ∈ P_n and V_{n+1} ⊆ V_n for all n has nonempty intersection, must the Wijsman hyperspace (2^X, T_W(d)) be pseudocomplete? Likewise, if X is subcompact or base-compact in the Amsterdam sense, i.e. regular and having an open base B such that every regular filterbase, respectively every centered family, contained in B has nonempty intersection, must (2^X, T_W(d)) be subcompact or base-compact, respectively?
justification: The draft unambiguously matches Section 3’s associated open question on completeness-type properties. In the introduction, the paper says its second basic problem concerns whether a Wijsman topology induced by a completely metrizable metric has completeness-type properties. Section 3 then frames Problem 3.1 in exactly those terms, narrows attention to non-closed-hereditary candidates, recalls the Amsterdam properties and the definition of pseudocompleteness, and finally states Question 3.11 with exactly the three property-preservation implications that your draft asks about. No equivalent reformulation of Question 3.11 is proved nearby, so the faithful target is the question itself.
